CULTURE AT SCRIBD, INC.

We support a culture where our employees can be real and be bold; where we debate and commit as we embrace plot twists; and where every employee is empowered to take action as we prioritize the customer.

Occasional in-person attendance is required for all Scribd, Inc. employees, regardless of location.

So what are we looking for in new team members? At Scribd, Inc., we hire for “GRIT.” Traditionally defined as the intersection of passion and perseverance toward long-term goals, GRIT reflects the mindset we expect from every employee. For us, it also serves as a practical framework for how we work: setting and achieving Goals, delivering Results within your role, contributing Innovative ideas and solutions, and strengthening the broader Team through collaboration and attitude.

This posting reflects an approved, open position within the organization.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Premium is the Scribd Inc. pillar behind two reading products: Everand, the audiobook and ebook subscription app, and Fable, the social app where readers track, discuss and discover books. Helping readers find their next book is central to both, so search and recommendations sit at the heart of the products.

You'll join Premium's new Discovery squad. It's a small, dedicated group of recommendations, search, applied research and ML engineers working full time on discovery for Everand and Fable. The squad works closely with Orion, Scribd's ML platform team. Orion runs the feature store, model registry, embedding-based retrieval and model serving behind discovery across Scribd, Slideshare and Everand.

ROLE OVERVIEW

We're looking for a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to own recommendations for Fable and grow into the technical lead for Premium recommendations.

Fable's recommender today is a collaborative-filtering model built in house. It has served readers well, but it has no real-time signals and no learned ranking, and it can't recommend to new or lapsed readers. Your first big project is to move Fable onto Orion, so Fable and Everand share a modern recommendation stack.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

- Lead the migration of Fable's recommendations onto Orion, covering data, features, training, serving and experiments, while keeping today's recommendations running.

- Extend Orion's rankers, feature store and embedding-based retrieval to support Fable, in partnership with the Orion ML platform team.

- Own the health of Fable's recommendation systems in production: quality, latency, cost and on-call.

- Bring Fable's social signals (shelves, ratings, reviews, book clubs, reader similarity) into recommendations for both Fable and Everand.

- Design and analyze A/B tests with product managers and analysts to decide what ships.

- Act as technical lead for Premium recommendations. Shape the roadmap with product managers, and see work that depends on other teams' systems through to delivery.

- Raise the bar on engineering practice in the squad through design reviews, code quality and operational readiness.

TECH YOU'LL WORK WITH

You'll work across two stacks: Fable's on Google Cloud and Orion's on AWS.

- Fable: Python (FastAPI, Django), PostgreSQL, BigQuery, Kubernetes, Google Cloud including Vertex AI

- Orion and Everand: Python, Go and gRPC, Ruby on Rails, Databricks and Spark, Airflow, AWS SageMaker, Weaviate for embedding-based retrieval, feature store and model registry

- Infrastructure: AWS (EKS, ECS, Lambda, SQS, ElastiCache), Datadog, Terraform

REQUIREMENTS

MUST HAVE

- 5+ years as a professional ML or software engineer, with a track record of shipping production ML systems.

- Hands-on experience building and running recommender systems in production, such as collaborative filtering or matrix factorization, two-tower or embedding retrieval, and learned ranking.

- Experience with large-scale data processing (Spark, Databricks, BigQuery or similar).

- Experience on at least one major cloud (AWS or GCP), including deploying services on containers (Kubernetes, ECS or similar).

- Experience designing and analyzing online experiments.

- A record of leading projects that depend on other teams, and of working directly with product managers.

- Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, or equivalent professional experience.

NICE TO HAVE

- Google Cloud experience, especially Vertex AI and BigQuery.

- Experience migrating or replacing a production ML system while keeping it running.

- Social or graph-based recommendations, such as user similarity, follows or groups.

- Search and semantic retrieval (Elasticsearch, Vertex AI Search, vector databases).

- Experience on consumer apps for reading, media or social.

## About Capstan Medical

At Capstan Medical, we're building one of the most exciting and innovative companies in medtech: a first-of-its-kind robotic platform for minimally invasive heart valve treatment.

Our team combines surgical robotics, catheter-based delivery, and next-generation implants to turn complex procedures into safer, lower-stress solutions for patients and clinicians. We're a collaborative, hands-on team that moves fast, wears multiple hats, and believes the best ideas can come from anyone.

Based in Santa Cruz, our workspace blends Bay Area innovation with a lifestyle near trails, beaches, and open space—a great place to do meaningful, career-defining work.

### About the Role

**Teach a heart valve robot to see where it is.**

We're hiring a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to join our robotics and controls team. You'll help our robot understand where its devices are inside the patient, using intraprocedural imaging such as fluoroscopy and echocardiography. That means building perception for image-to-robot registration and pose estimation, and taking it from research into a clinical system.

This is not a model-in-a-notebook role. Your work runs on a real-time robotic system, informs what physicians see during the procedure, and ships under FDA design controls.

You'll also help shape how we collect, organize, and learn from our robot and imaging data, and use it to improve our device models and controllers. You'll have a large say in how ML is done here, from the tools and standards we adopt to which problems we tackle first, and you'll be the person the rest of the team turns to for ML judgment.

### What You'll Do

* Develop methods to register intraprocedural imaging, such as fluoroscopy and echocardiography, to the robot.
    
* Estimate the pose of catheters and implants from medical images.
    
* Combine image-based estimates with robot kinematics and other sensing, and quantify the uncertainty of each estimate.
    
* Build data pipelines that capture, align, label, and version imaging and robot data for training and evaluation.
    
* Use simulation and synthetic data where real clinical data is limited.
    
* Fit and improve models of device behavior from data, and work with controls engineers to turn them into better control.
    
* Work with clinical engineers and physicians to learn what the images show, what matters in the procedure, and what accuracy is good enough.
    
* Read the literature, prototype what looks promising, and tell us plainly what works on our data and what doesn't.
    
* Deploy models on the robot and meet real-time latency budgets.
    
* Write the validation, test datasets, and design documentation that let learned components pass FDA design controls.
    

### Skills

* **Real-World Machine Learning:** You've taken models out of notebooks and into products that run on real data, with all its noise, drift, and edge cases.
    
* **Computer Vision:** Strong background in classical and learned computer vision, especially pose estimation, segmentation, tracking, or 2D/3D registration.
    
* **3D Geometry:** Solid grasp of rigid transforms, rotations, camera projection models, and calibration.
    
* **Programming:** Strong Python and PyTorch skills. Comfortable reading and writing C++.
    
* **Data Engineering:** You build pipelines, datasets, and evaluation harnesses that others can trust and reuse.
    
* **Research and Prototyping:** You keep up with recent papers, can tell which ideas will survive contact with our data, and enjoy turning them into working prototypes.
    
* **Problem-Solving:** Comfortable with high ambiguity. You can take a fuzzy goal, break it into experiments, and pick a direction without a spec.
    
* **Communication:** Excellent communicator who can explain ML clearly to controls engineers, clinical engineers, and physicians, document work effectively, and help the team decide when a model is good enough to trust.
    

### Requirements

* MS in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, or a related field. PhD is a plus.
    
* 4+ years of professional experience in computer vision or machine learning, classical or learned, including at least one system shipped to production on real-world data.
    
* Experience working with scarce, noisy, or expensive data, using synthetic data, augmentation, self-supervision, or physics priors to make up for it.
    
* Experience building ML on data from physical systems such as robots, cameras, medical imaging, or sensors.
    
* Ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment and own problems end-to-end.
    
* Ability to work onsite 3–4 days per week, split flexibly between our Santa Cruz, CA and West Menlo Park, CA offices, with at least 1 day per week in Santa Cruz.
    

### Preferred Qualifications

* Ultrasound or echocardiography experience, strongly preferred. Fluoroscopy or X-ray experience is also valuable, including 2D/3D registration or digitally reconstructed radiographs.
    
* Experience tracking catheters, needles, surgical tools, or continuum robots in images.
    
* Sensor fusion and state estimation, such as Kalman filters or factor graphs.
    
* System identification or learned dynamics for control, including residual models on top of physics.
    
* Robotics software experience with ROS/ROS2 and on-device inference under latency constraints (ONNX, TensorRT).
    
* Data platform and MLOps experience, including practices like dataset versioning and experiment tracking.
    
* Medical device or safety-critical background, including validating ML under FDA design controls.
    
* Experience as an early ML engineer on a team, setting up the tools, data practices, and evaluation that others build on.
    
* Publications at venues such as MICCAI, IPCAI, CVPR, ICRA, or IROS.
    

### Why join us:

* We offer a fun, fast-paced, collaborative environment where you will be working on transformational technologies in the cardiac healthcare space.
    

* We offer outstanding benefits with medical, dental, and vision covered at 100% for you and your family, as well as flex time off.
    

* We thrive in our work-hard, play-hard environment. Bring your bike or running shoes if you’d like or just be ready to enjoy a fun office outing. We enjoy time inside the office and out!

ABOUT MERCOR

Mercor’s mission is to organize human intelligence for the AI economy. We build the infrastructure that enables frontier AI labs and enterprises to train, evaluate, and improve AI on real-world professional work. More than five million experts have joined our network, and we pay out over $5 million daily for their knowledge and expertise.

We built our training and evaluation infrastructure alongside the world’s leading AI labs. Now, we’re bringing those capabilities to enterprises across industries, enabling them to train, evaluate, and improve AI using their own expertise and standards. Our APEX benchmarks measure how AI performs on economically valuable work, while our enterprise evaluations and post-training capabilities turn those insights into measurable improvements across real-world workflows.

Our work sits at the intersection of frontier AI, human expertise, and real-world application. We’re solving problems few companies have encountered, with the opportunity to influence what the world’s most advanced AI systems become capable of doing. We’re looking for people who bring different perspectives, take ownership, exercise sound judgment, and hold themselves to an exceptionally high standard. You’ll have the opportunity to do consequential work alongside talented colleagues who challenge one another, collaborate openly, and share a commitment to excellence.

Mercor is profitable and recently raised a $750 million Series D at a $20 billion valuation. We work in person five days a week in San Francisco, New York, and London.

About the Role:

Frontier AI companies are increasingly bottlenecked on expert judgment — capturing it reliably, validating it at scale, and turning it into durable model behavior. This role sits at the center of that problem.

You'll build the ML systems that power Mercor's Frontier Data Products: the infrastructure that scores, validates, and improves complex work products where correctness is rarely binary and labels are often noisy, delayed, or disputed. A single job can stay live for days, interleaving model inference, automated checks, expert review, disagreement resolution, and feedback loops. Your work determines how models reason over ambiguous inputs, when they should defer to humans, how quality is measured, and how feedback compounds into better systems over time.

This is applied ML product engineering under real production constraints — incomplete ground truth, shifting requirements, latency and cost tradeoffs, and workflows where a silent model failure corrupts the final output. It is not an offline benchmarks role.

What You'll Do

• Build ML systems that score, validate, and improve complex work products where correctness is nuanced and labels are imperfect.

• Design evaluation frameworks for ambiguous tasks where ground truth is partial, delayed, or disputed.

• Build feedback loops that turn review, disagreement, correction, and adjudication into measurable model and system improvements.

• Own production ML behavior end-to-end: precision/recall tradeoffs, regression detection, drift, latency, cost, and explainability.

• Improve model quality using the right tool for the job — prompting, fine-tuning, retrieval, active learning, heuristics, and error analysis.

• Partner with backend engineers to integrate inference into durable, long-running workflows without sacrificing debuggability or human oversight.

What Makes This Role Different

• The architecture is not set — early engineers will define how quality is measured, how models and humans interact, where automation is trusted, and how the system compounds over time.

• The feedback loop is short: shipping a model behavior change directly and visibly affects what customers receive.

• You're working on a strategically central product area at Mercor at a moment when frontier AI companies have no good solution to the problem you're solving.

Day-to-Day

• Moving fast on a young, high-ownership codebase where your decisions have long-term architectural weight.

• Operating across models, data, backend systems, and product surfaces — context switching is the default, not the exception.

• Debugging production ML failures in live, long-running workflows where silent errors matter.

• Working closely with backend engineers on a stack of Python, Temporal, Postgres, AWS, and LiteLLM.

• Balancing automation confidence with human review — knowing when to defer is as important as knowing when to ship.

What We're Looking For

• Track record of shipping ML systems that improved a real product, workflow, or business metric.

• Strong instincts for model quality, evaluation design, error analysis, and production failure modes.

• Comfort operating in ambiguous problem spaces where labels are imperfect and correctness evolves.

• Sound judgment about when to reach for prompting, fine-tuning, heuristics, retrieval, human review, or a simpler product constraint.

• Solid engineering fundamentals across the full ML stack — not just modeling.

• Familiarity with LLM applications, model-assisted workflows, evaluation frameworks, or human-in-the-loop ML is a strong plus.

You're likely someone who:

• Has 4+ years of experience

• Defaults to simple, inspectable ML systems that improve quickly and fail in understandable ways — not the most impressive architecture.

• Gets uncomfortable when a model ships without a clear evaluation story.

• Can hold ambiguity without paralysis and make reasonable bets with incomplete information.

• Cares about the real-world output of the system, not just the benchmark.
